alt.en: A page of printed music headed "Skye Boat Song." and "(Jacobite.)". At the left, "Words by Harold Boulton"; at the right, "Four bars taken down from Hebridean boatmen, four bars added by A. C. Macleod" and "Malcolm Lawson". A voice line and piano part in 6/8 run under the direction "With animation and well accented", the words beginning "Speed bonnie boat like a bird on the wing", with a footnote in small italic type at the foot of the page.
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el encabezado "Skye Boat Song." y "(Jacobite.)". A la izquierda, "Words by Harold Boulton"; a la derecha, "Four bars taken down from Hebridean boatmen, four bars added by A. C. Macleod" y "Malcolm Lawson". Una línea de voz y una parte de piano en 6/8 van bajo la indicación "With animation and well accented", con la letra que empieza "Speed bonnie boat like a bird on the wing", y una nota al pie en cursiva pequeña al final de la página.

caption.en: The song's first page in Songs of the North, in the undated Cramer reprint our arrangement is read from: Boulton's words, an air of "four bars taken down from Hebridean boatmen, four bars added by A. C. Macleod", and Malcolm Lawson's piano part.
caption.es: La primera página de la canción en Songs of the North, en la reimpresión de Cramer sin fecha de la que leemos nuestro arreglo: la letra de Boulton, una melodía de "cuatro compases tomados de barqueros de las Hébridas, cuatro compases añadidos por A. C. Macleod" y la parte de piano de Malcolm Lawson.

date: undated Cramer reprint, catalogued 19-- (record date 1900); the book was reviewed as new in July 1885
source: A. C. Macleod and Harold Boulton, editors, music arranged by Malcolm Lawson, Songs of the North, vol. I (London: J. B. Cramer & Co., undated later printing; earlier published by Field and Tuer), "Skye Boat Song (Jacobite)", p. 18
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: M1746 B78 S6 19--, barcode 31761034118778; Internet Archive 31761034118778, image n37
licenceEvidence: Book reviewed as new in July 1885 (Illustrated London News, 11 July 1885); this copy an undated later Cramer printing. Everything on the page is by the song's own makers: words Harold Boulton (died 1935), air Anne Campbell Macleod (died 1921), arrangement Malcolm Lawson (died 1918). Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A sepia photograph along a high sea cliff of tall upright columns of dark rock standing on paler layered rock, with a rough slope of grass and broken stones in front and calm sea far below at the right. White lettering along the bottom reads "The Kilt Rock, Loch Staffin, Skye. 898. G.W.W."
alt.es: Fotografía en sepia a lo largo de un acantilado alto sobre el mar, con altas columnas verticales de roca oscura sobre capas de roca más clara, una ladera áspera de hierba y piedras sueltas delante y el mar en calma muy abajo, a la derecha. Unas letras blancas al pie dicen "The Kilt Rock, Loch Staffin, Skye. 898. G.W.W."

caption.en: The sea cliffs of Kilt Rock, by Loch Staffin on the Isle of Skye, photographed by George Washington Wilson of Aberdeen between about 1860 and 1880; Skye is the island the boat makes for in the song's chorus.
caption.es: Los acantilados de Kilt Rock, junto a Loch Staffin, en la isla de Skye, fotografiados por George Washington Wilson, de Aberdeen, entre 1860 y 1880 aproximadamente; Skye es la isla hacia la que navega la barca en el estribillo de la canción.

source: George Washington Wilson, "The Kilt Rock, Loch Staffin, Skye" (title on object), albumen print on card; cropped to the print
licenceEvidence: Rijksmuseum data record https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/200408231: "rights": https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark 1.0); creator George Washington Wilson; date "ca. 1860 - ca. 1880". Wilson died 1893 (see rights.md).

alt.en: A printed book page, page 239, with the running head "Skye Boat-Song." A paragraph of text ends "the music by kind permission of the publishers", then comes the heading "Skye Boat-Song." and four lines of melody with words under the notes, from "Speed, bonnie boat, like a bird on the wing" to "Fol-low they will not dare", with "Thunder-clouds rend the air" in the third line. A footnote at the foot names a book on Flora Macdonald.
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro, página 239, con el titulillo "Skye Boat-Song." Un párrafo de texto termina con "the music by kind permission of the publishers"; siguen el encabezado "Skye Boat-Song." y cuatro líneas de melodía con la letra bajo las notas, desde "Speed, bonnie boat, like a bird on the wing" hasta "Fol-low they will not dare", con "Thunder-clouds rend the air" en la tercera línea. Una nota al pie cita un libro sobre Flora Macdonald.

caption.en: John Stuart Blackie's Scottish Song (Edinburgh, 1889) prints the tune with Boulton's words, by permission of the publishers of Songs of the North, and sings "Thunder-clouds rend the air" where "Thunderclaps" is sung today.
caption.es: Scottish Song, de John Stuart Blackie (Edimburgo, 1889), imprime la melodía con la letra de Boulton, con permiso de los editores de Songs of the North, y canta "Thunder-clouds rend the air" (nubes de tormenta desgarran el aire) donde hoy se canta "Thunderclaps" (truenos).

source: John Stuart Blackie, Scottish Song: Its Wealth, Wisdom, and Social Significance (Edinburgh and London: William Blackwood and Sons, 1889), "Skye Boat-Song", p. 239
library: University of California Libraries (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: GLAD-17148114 (nrlf_ucb); Internet Archive scottishsongitsw00blacrich, image n254
licenceEvidence: Published Edinburgh and London, 1889. John Stuart Blackie died 1895; the song's words are Harold Boulton's (died 1935) and its air Anne Campbell Macleod's (died 1921).
